A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TempMe, and their main text, figures and tables are readable and directly comparable. However, v1 ends after the references despite referring to Appendices A-D; v2 includes those appendices. Changes involving the unavailable earlier supplementary material cannot be fully established.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, computational measurements, component ablations and UMT-based retrieval/QA experiments in Tables 1-9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and includes additional empirical results and analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: The comparable method descriptions retain LoRA adaptation, progressive image/clip merging, alternating bipartite matching, cross-clip positional embeddings and intra-clip merging. v2 clarifies retention ratios and implementation settings without establishing a changed algorithm, architecture or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MSRVTT, ActivityNet, DiDeMo and LSMDC for retrieval, and MSR-QA for the UMT-based QA experiment. Video-to-text evaluation is already explicitly described in v1. Different frame counts and additional backbone configurations do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds DGL-T to the MSRVTT ViT-B/32 comparison, alongside the retained DGL variant, now labeled DGL-L. VoP's F+C designation clarifies an existing comparator. The remaining matched main-text comparator sets are retained; the added related-work discussion of DeCo does not constitute an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 5 extends the full-fine-tuning evaluation to inference memory. The stated AdamW optimizer, batch size 128 and standard 12/64-frame settings remain unchanged. Appendix C.7 also documents an 18-frame configuration, but its status relative to v1's unavailable appendix cannot be established. Expanded training-setting disclosures alone do not demonstrate changed experiments.

E4.justification: The component and functional ablations in Tables 8-9 retain their findings. v2 presents merging-strategy, positional-embedding, merging-hyperparameter, frame-sampling and qualitative analyses that v1 already announces in its unavailable Appendix C. v2 also includes a memory/18-frame analysis in C.7. Without the earlier appendix, the extent of genuinely added or revised analyses is uncertain.

E5.justification: Both Table 5 captions specify five experiments with different random seeds. No new confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting practices are evident in v2, including its appendices.

E6.justification: Table 2 exchanges the ViT-B/32 VoP and DGL recall rows: their R-Sums change from 194.4/194.8 to 194.8/194.4. MV-Adapter's ViT-B/16 R@1 changes from 46.2 to 46.0 and R-Sum from 202.1 to 200.1. DGL-T results and Table 5 inference-memory values are added, while Table 9 omits R@5/R@10 breakdowns. Matched TempMe benchmark scores remain unchanged. Earlier appendix results are unavailable for numerical comparison.

T1.justification: The shared token-count expressions and mathematical description of merging are unchanged. v2 Appendix A supplies attention, contrastive-loss and LoRA equations, but v1's referenced Appendix A is unavailable. Whether any formal definitions or mathematical reasoning were added or revised there cannot be determined.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that progressive temporal merging improves the efficiency and accuracy of CLIP-based retrieval and generalizes across efficient and full fine-tuning. The headline efficiency and performance claims are retained. v2 emphasizes the 0.50M trainable-parameter count already reported in v1 Table 2, rather than introducing a substantively different contribution.

C2.justification: The shared explanations attributing accuracy to temporal modeling and efficiency to token reduction remain stable. v2 discusses merging-strategy tradeoffs, limited inference-memory savings despite lower GFLOPs, and compatibility restrictions for specialized video encoders. Because v1 directs readers to unavailable Appendices C-D for analyses and limitations, the extent of new interpretation or qualification cannot be reliably assessed.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising a future code release to stating availability at a specific repository. Section 4.1 makes the learning rate, five-epoch schedule, LoRA rank, retention ratios and merging-layer schedules explicit. v2 also supplies dataset splits and memory-measurement hardware details. These improve accessible documentation, but v1's missing implementation appendix prevents treating every detail as newly introduced or as a changed setting.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of image versus video compression and clarifies TempMe's relationship to STA, TESTA and CLIP's separate frame-token sets. It adds citations such as Cap4Video, DeCo and additional tuning methods, while removing some adaptive-token-pruning references. The central positioning around efficient CLIP adaptation and temporal merging remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and parts of the introduction are rewritten around two efficiency challenges, related work gains image/video compression distinctions, and implementation and merging-strategy explanations receive more main-text space. Authors, affiliations, acknowledgments and citation style also change. The overall section sequence and most method and experimental exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figures 1-4 retain their substantive visual content. v2 adopts ICLR formatting, adds R@1 fields to Tables 1, 4 and 5, adds inference memory to Table 5, and compacts Tables 8-9 into adjacent displays with fewer columns. Rank headers change from MdR to MnR, consistent with the existing metric description. Earlier appendix displays are unavailable for comparison.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through a concrete code-access statement, clearer main-text implementation settings and inference-memory reporting that qualifies the efficiency benefits. The core method and matched TempMe results remain stable. Reduced ablation metric breakdowns slightly diminish detail, and the missing v1 appendices prevent crediting all supplementary material as new. The verified changes nevertheless support a limited overall improvement.
